plan.scope: Native FP32 implementation of the three locked lighting graphs; numerical equivalence and standalone timings, not Enfusion integration
plan.input_layout: Interleaved little-endian FP32: model features in serialized order, original scene-linear source RGB, alpha, valid flag (0 or 1)
plan.output_layout: Interleaved little-endian FP32: predicted log1p residual RGB, corrected scene-linear RGB, original alpha
plan.output_operation: max(expm1(source log1p RGB + residual), 0); invalid pixels preserve original source RGB exactly; alpha always preserved
plan.precision: FP32 weights, normalization, dense layers, activation and output; no quantization or retraining
plan.fixture_scope: Deterministic original feature/mask/color controls at each size; these are numerical workloads, not rendered quality comparisons
plan.rendered_cases: All 48 existing cross-courtyard test frames and both 32-frame regression paths, without rendering, fitting or candidate selection; compare native output against the retained CPU evaluation

bound_followup.reason: The initial RGB-only 4K shader produces one residual 0.2500000298023224, exceeding the defined 0.25 bound despite passing numerical error tolerances.
bound_followup.change: Explicitly clamp the shader tanh residual to the existing model bound. No weights, normalization, model selection, numerical tolerances or fidelity limits change.
bound_followup.verification: Repeat all 21 numerical size/variant checks after this shader change; then run the originally planned 1440p benchmark and all 112 rendered frames.
bound_followup.retention: Keep the initial disk-write failure and GPU bound failure. Generated random input buffers may be removed only after byte-exact regeneration, retaining their recipes and source snapshots. All GPU outputs remain. Rendered source EXRs remain; their derived packed transfer buffers are temporary.
bound_followup.scope: Standalone native model correctness only; supported Enfusion inputs/execution and actual-Arma fidelity remain required.
